_readme: TEMPLATE for <runtime root>/config/offsite_scopes.json — the scope declaration
cosmos_offsite_clock reads. It is NOT read from here; copy it to the config role.
Nothing in COSMOS guesses a source tree: an absent declaration is a typed refusal
(NO_SCOPES), because a backup that quietly covers a plausible-but-wrong tree is the
green-log defect this whole module exists to refuse.
'name' becomes the R2 key prefix and is validated like a manifest key — no absolute
paths, no '..'. Each push lands under <name>/<YYYYmmddTHHMMSS>/, so a push never
overwrites its predecessor and nothing is ever deleted from the bucket by COSMOS.
ORDER MATTERS: scopes are pushed in the order listed, smallest first, because a 65
GiB monolith that refuses at 90% restarts from zero. Roll out one scope at a time.
MEASURED SIZES (2026-08-31, docs/R2_OFFSITE_PLAN.md §3): cosmos/ 220 files /
V:\A 55,864 / 29.84 GiB. The three WISHLIST trees hold 2,143 files past MAX_PATH;
they are covered (test_longpath_r2.py) but they are why the first push is slow.
SECRETS: a scope containing key material REFUSES with SECRETS_IN_SCOPE before a
byte moves — this target is unencrypted and there is no override flag. Exclude the
offending file or build encryption at rest; do not add a bypass.
The 'trees' entry below is commented out by being named '_staged_later': add it to
'scopes' only after the cosmos/ push has been proven against the real bucket.
F-54 orchestrator state is NOT a live/state wholesale scope (that dir holds
mailboxes and dispatch receipts). cosmos_state_offsite.py packs a whitelist
(SEED.json, SEED.decl.json, inflight.jsonl, motif_tracker.json) into
work/_delme_state_offsite/<stamp>/payload and pushes THAT tree. Without dests
and without the R2 credential the packer's tick REFUSES NO_OFFSITE_ROUTE.
